# Codelessly layout documents: a guide for authors

This guide is for writing Codelessly user interfaces directly as JSON: screens, their layout, their look, their
data and their behavior. It describes `codelessly_api` 24.0.0, the data model the Codelessly SDK renders. Every
example on this page is checked by a test: it decodes, passes strict validation and was rendered with the SDK.

The rest of the reference is generated from the declarations in the code, so it lists every node type, prop,
field, enum value, trigger, action and formula function with its type and default:
[node types](#page-nodes), [layout](#page-layout), [decoration](#page-decoration),
[value types, models and enums](#page-values), [behaviors](#page-behaviors), [triggers](#page-triggers),
[actions](#page-actions), [bindings](#page-bindings), [formula functions](#page-formulas),
[variables, conditions and scripts](#page-variables-conditions-scripts). `catalog.json` holds the same
information as data and `document.schema.json` is a JSON Schema for a document.

<a id="guide-document"></a>
## 1. The document

A layout document is one JSON object. It holds one or more **canvases** (screens) and all their nodes in a
single flat map.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema` | Always 2 (`kSchemaVersion`). |
| `id` | The layout's id (optional). |
| `roots` | Canvas ids, in order: the screens of this page. |
| `nodes` | Every node, by id: `{"<id>": {"type": ..., ...}}`. A node's id is its key here. |
| `variables` | Variables per scope: `{"<canvas id>" \| "page_variables": [variable, ...]}`. |
| `conditions` | Conditions per canvas: `{"<canvas id>": [condition, ...]}`. |
| `scripts` | The layout's scripts (JavaScript), a list of script objects. |
| `breakpoints` | The project's breakpoints: `[{"id", "name", "minWidth", "width", "height"}]`; absent: the defaults. |

The smallest useful document: a canvas whose `body` slot holds a column with two texts.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["home"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "slots": {"body": "page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["title", "body"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 12}
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 34}},
      "props": {"text": "Hello", "style": {"fontSize": 28, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "body": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
      "props": {
        "text": "A column with two texts, filling the screen's width.",
        "style": {"fontSize": 15, "height": 1.4, "color": "#FF4B5563"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Nothing else is needed: every key not written takes its default. A document is a **page**; a site with several
pages is either one document with several canvases in `roots`, or several documents (one file each) checked and
rendered together ([section 6](#guide-screens)).

<a id="guide-nodes"></a>
## 2. Nodes, ids and children

`nodes` maps each node's **id** to the node. The id is the map key; do not repeat it inside the node. Ids are
any text; use short readable ones (`hero-title`), and keep them unique across all documents of a site, because
actions, conditions, diagnostics and the render command name nodes by id.

Every node has a `type` (one of the [node types](#page-nodes)). Its keys:

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | `String` | The node type (a key of `nodeTypes`). Required. |
| `name` | `String` |  |
| `key` | `String` | The node's name within the tree it was inserted with, unique in that tree (`"content"`): a stable handle the tree's own actions and states name it by before it has an id, kept so an export gives the tree back with its keys. Empty for none; it doesn't affect rendering. |
| `children` | `List<String>` | Ordered child ids, for types that take children. |
| `slots` | `Map<String, String>` | Named children, slot → node id, for types with slots. |
| `layout` | `Layout` | How the node sizes itself and sits in its parent (see layout). |
| `decoration` | `Decoration` | Fills, strokes, radius, shadows, blurs, clip (see decoration). |
| `props` | `Map` | The node type's own parameters (see nodeTypes). |
| `bind` | `Map<String, String>` | Bound properties: a binding path (`visible`, `props.text`, `layout.width`, `decoration.fills.<paintId>`; see `BindPaths` and DESIGN.md §5.1) → an expression (`${user.name}`, `${= qty * 2}`). |
| `actions` | `List<Reaction>` | Reactions: `{"trigger": {...}, "actions": [...]}` (see triggers, actions). |
| `component` | `ComponentLink` | The component this node is the main node of, or the top node of an instance of (DESIGN.md §4.2). |
| `visible` | bool | Default `true`.  |
| `opacity` | double | Default `1`.  |
| behaviors |  | Flat keys for what a node does beyond layout and paint: `motion`, `scale`, `animations`, `transitions`, `inkWell`, `states`, `tooltip`, `ignorePointer`, `zoomable`, `floating`, `hero`, `flightKey`, `flight`, `draggable`, `dropTarget`, `track`, `dismissible`, `pan`, `reorderHandle`, `reveal`, `strokePath`, `typewriter`, `particles`, `textDirection`, `flip`, `tilt`, `transformGesture`, `sticky`, `viewProgress`, `measure`, `customPaint` ([behaviors](#page-behaviors)). |

**The tree is made of ids.** A parent lists its children's ids; a child does not name its parent:

- `children` is an ordered list of ids, for the types that take children: `row`, `column`, `stack`, `listView`,
  `gridView`, `pageView`, `variance` and a few more (the "Children" column below).
- `slots` maps a slot name to one id, for types with named places: a `canvas` has `body`, `appBar`,
  `floatingActionButton` and `bottomNavigationBar`; a `listTile` has `leading`, `title`, `subtitle`, `trailing`.
- Every node except a canvas has exactly one parent. A node listed under two parents, or not listed under any,
  is an error or a warning in validation. To show the same thing twice, write two nodes with their own ids.
- `roots` lists the canvases. A canvas is never a child.

There is no `Padding`, `SizedBox`, `Expanded`, `Positioned`, `Align`, `DecoratedBox` or `Opacity` node: those
Flutter wrappers are fields of the node itself (`layout`, `decoration`, `opacity`). A "card" is one `column` with
a fill, a radius and padding, not three nested widgets.

| Type | Flutter | Children | Decoration |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`canvas`](#node-canvas) | `Scaffold` | slots: `body`, `appBar`, `floatingActionButton`, `bottomNavigationBar` | yes |
| [`stack`](#node-stack) | `Stack` | `children` | yes |
| [`box`](#node-box) | `Container` | none | yes |

<a id="guide-layout"></a>
## 3. Layout

`layout` says how big a node is and where it sits in its parent. Full field list: [layout](#page-layout).

### Width and height

Each axis has a **mode** and a **number**:

| JSON | Mode | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `120` | fixed | Exactly 120. |
| `{"hug": 120}` | hug | The size of the content (a text's lines, a row's children plus padding). |
| `{"fill": 120}` | fill | All the room the parent gives: the free space along a row's or column's main axis (shared by `flex`), the whole cross axis of a row or column, the whole box of a stack or canvas slot. |
| `{"flexible": 120}` | flexible | Up to 120, less if a row or column runs out of room (only along a row's or column's main axis). |

The number is the **design size**: the size of a fixed node, and the size used when a mode cannot apply (a fill
inside something that scrolls on that axis, for instance). For `hug` and `fill` it does not limit the size:
`{"fill": 760}` in a 1300 wide column is 1300 wide. Write the size you expect, and use
`"constraints": {"maxWidth": 760}` to cap it.

**A node without `width` or `height` is fixed at 0 and draws nothing.** Validation warns (`zero_size`). Give every
node both, except a `canvas` (its size is the screen's) and a `spacer`.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["sizing"],
  "nodes": {
    "sizing": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 400, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["hugText", "fillBox", "bar"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 400}, "height": {"fill": 400}, "padding": 10},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 8}
    },
    "hugText": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "As wide as its text", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "color": "#FF000000"}}
    },
    "fillBox": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 380}, "height": 24},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFEF4444"}]}
    },
    "bar": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["one", "two", "fixed"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 380}, "height": 40},
      "props": {"spacing": 10}
    },
    "one": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 100}, "height": {"fill": 40}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF22C55E"}]}
    },
    "two": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 200}, "height": {"fill": 40}, "flex": 2},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF3B82F6"}]}
    },
    "fixed": {"type": "box", "layout": {"width": 60, "height": 20}, "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF9CA3AF"}]}}
  }
}
```

In this example the text hugs its content, the red box fills the column's width, and in the row the green box
and the blue box share the free space 1 : 2 (`flex`) beside a fixed grey box.

### Rows and columns

`row` and `column` lay their children along their **main axis** (horizontal for a row, vertical for a column)
with these props: `mainAxisAlignment` (default `start`), `crossAxisAlignment` (default **`center`**: children are
centered across the axis unless you say `start`, `end` or `stretch`), `spacing` (gap between children, default
0), `wrap` (flow onto new lines, like `Wrap`; `runSpacing` between lines), `squeezeChildren` (default true: if
the children do not fit, they shrink toward their content size instead of overflowing).

Under a row or column a child may also set, in its own `layout`:

- `flex`: its share of the free space when its main-axis size is `fill` or `flexible` (default 1);
- `align`: its alignment within its slot, as `[x, y]` from -1 to 1 or a name (`"centerRight"`); the node's box
  then spans the slot and its content sits at that alignment;
- `squeezable`: a hugging child that may shrink below its content when room runs out.

### Padding, margin, constraints, aspect ratio

- `padding` is space inside the node's box, around its content and children; `margin` is space outside it.
  Both are a number (all sides) or a list of **four** numbers `[left, top, right, bottom]`. A list of two is not
  read (it becomes 0 on every side; validation reports it).
- `constraints`: `{"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"}`, each optional. A `fill` width with
  `"maxWidth": 1100` gives a content column that grows with the window up to 1100; its parent's
  `crossAxisAlignment` (center by default) places it.
- `aspectRatio`: width / height the node keeps (`1.5`).
- `rotation`: degrees, clockwise, about the center; layout is unchanged.

### Stacks: placing children freely

A `stack` places each child by its `layout.x` and `layout.y`, measured inside the stack's padding to the child's
margin box. Each axis takes one of:

| JSON | Placement |
|---|---|
| `{"start": 16}` (or just `16`) | 16 from the left (x) or top (y) |
| `{"end": 16}` | 16 from the right or bottom |
| `{"start": 16, "end": 16}` | Stretched between: 16 from both edges. Works for fixed and fill sizes; a `hug` size keeps its own size and sits at the start. |
| `{"align": 0}` | Aligned like `Align`: -1 start, 0 center, 1 end |
| `{"relative": 300}` | 300 from the start at the stack's design size, keeping its share of the free space as the stack resizes |

`x`, `y` mean nothing under a row or column, and `flex`, `align` nothing under a stack: validation warns
(`layout_field_ignored`). Children paint in order: later ones on top.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["board"],
  "nodes": {
    "board": {"type": "canvas", "slots": {"body": "stage"}, "layout": {"width": 400, "height": 300}},
    "stage": {
      "type": "stack",
      "children": ["photo", "badge", "caption"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 400}, "height": {"fill": 300}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFE5E7EB"}]}
    },
    "photo": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 200, "height": 120, "x": {"align": 0}, "y": {"align": 0}},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [
          {
            "type": "linear",
            "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FF6366F1"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#FFEC4899"}]
          }
        ],
        "radius": 16
      }
    },
    "badge": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 48, "height": 48, "x": {"end": 16}, "y": {"start": 16}},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF59E0B"}], "shape": "circle"}
    },
    "caption": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}, "x": {"start": 16, "end": 16}, "y": {"end": 16}},
      "props": {
        "text": "Pinned 16 px from the left, right and bottom",
        "textAlign": "center",
        "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF374151"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Which modes each parent allows (from the parents' own rules):

| Parent | Width may be | Height may be |
|---|---|---|
| `row` | fixed, fill, flexible, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, flexible, hug |
| `row` with {"wrap":true} | fixed, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` with {"scrollable":true} | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, hug |
| `row` with {"scrollable":true,"scrollDirection":"horizontal"} | fixed, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `stack` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `canvas` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `listView` | fill | fixed, hug |
| `listView` with {"itemExtent":80} | fill | fill |
| `gridView` | fill | fill |
| `pageView` | fill | fill |

<a id="guide-decoration"></a>
## 4. Decoration

`decoration` paints the node's box (types with "box decoration" above). Full list: [decoration](#page-decoration).

- `fills`: a list of paints, bottom to top. `{"color": "#FF2563EB"}` is a solid color. A gradient is
  `{"type": "linear" | "radial" | "sweep" | "diamond", "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": ...}, {"position": 1, "color": ...}]}`;
  a linear gradient runs left to right unless it has `"begin"` and `"end"` (alignments, `[0, -1]` to `[0, 1]` is
  top to bottom) or a `transform`. An image is `{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "...", "fit": "cover"}}`. A paint
  without `type` is an image if it has `image`, a linear gradient if it has `stops`, else a solid color.
- `strokes`: paints for the border, with `strokeWidth` (default 1), `strokeAlign` (`inside`, `center`,
  `outside`), `strokeSides` (`all`, `bottom`, `topBottom`...) and `dashPattern` (`[6, 4]`). `strokeWidth` without
  `strokes` draws nothing.
- `radius`: corner radius: a number, `[x, y]`, or `[topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft]`.
- `shape`: `"circle"` paints a circle the box's shortest side across.
- `effects`: shadows and blurs, each `{"type": "dropShadow" | "innerShadow" | "layerBlur" | "backgroundBlur", ...}`
  with `color`, `offset` (`[dx, dy]`), `blurRadius`, `spreadRadius`. **An effect needs its `type`**; without it the
  effect is dropped.
- `clip`: `"antiAlias"` (or `hardEdge`) clips the content to the rounded box.

Colors are always `"#AARRGGBB"` (alpha first: `#FF` opaque, `#80` half, `#00` invisible) or `"#RRGGBB"` (opaque).
`"#FFF"`, `"rgb(...)"` and names are not read.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["deco"],
  "nodes": {
    "deco": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "row"},
      "layout": {"width": 520, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF9FAFB"}]}
    },
    "row": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["card", "gradient", "outlined"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 520}, "height": {"fill": 200}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 24, "mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "card": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}],
        "radius": 12,
        "effects": [{"type": "dropShadow", "color": "#33000000", "offset": [0, 4], "blurRadius": 16}]
      }
    },
    "gradient": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [
          {
            "type": "radial",
            "stops": [{"position": 0, "color": "#FFFDE68A"}, {"position": 1, "color": "#FFF97316"}]
          }
        ],
        "radius": [24, 4, 24, 4]
      }
    },
    "outlined": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 140, "height": 120},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "strokeWidth": 2, "dashPattern": [6, 4], "radius": 12}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-text"></a>
## 5. Text

A `text` node has `props.text` and `props.style`, a [TextStyle](#type-TextStyle):
`fontSize`, `fontWeight` (100–900), `fontFamily`, `color`, `height` (line height as a multiple of the font size),
`letterSpacing`, `decoration` (`underline`...), `fontStyle` (`italic`). Also `textAlign`, `maxLines` and
`overflow` (`ellipsis`).

What a text looks like when the style leaves something out:

- **No `color`: the text is painted white.** On a light background it is invisible. Always set `color`.
- No `fontSize`: 12. No `height`: 1.33 × the font size per line. No `fontWeight`: 400. No `letterSpacing`: 0.
- No `fontFamily`: the platform's default font (Roboto on Android and the web).

Sizing: a single line `{"hug": n}` × `{"hug": n}`; a paragraph `{"fill": n}` wide (it wraps) × `{"hug": n}` high.
A fixed height shorter than the lines clips them (the render command reports `text_clipped`).

`runs` style parts of the text: `[{"start": 0, "end": 5, "style": {"fontWeight": 700}}]` (character offsets, end
exclusive), merged over `style`; a run may carry a `"link"` URL. `text` may contain expressions:
`"Hello, ${user.name}"` ([section 8](#guide-variables)).

<a id="guide-screens"></a>
## 6. Screens and navigation

Each canvas in `roots` is a screen, unless canvases are grouped: canvases with the same `props.screen` are **one
screen**, one canvas per breakpoint ([section 7](#guide-responsive)). A canvas is the Flutter `Scaffold` of its
screen: put the page content in its `body` slot, usually a column filling it (`{"fill": n}` both ways). Its
`decoration.fills` is the page background. Its `layout` width and height are its design size; on a device the
canvas takes the screen's size.

Going from screen to screen is an action ([section 10](#guide-reactions)):
`{"type": "navigate", "to": "<canvas id>"}` pushes the screen; `"mode": "pop"` goes back; `"replace"` and
`"reset"` replace the history. `to` names a canvas: for a screen with a canvas per breakpoint, name any of
them; the canvas shown is the one for the current width. `"params": {"id": "${item.id}"}` passes values the
destination reads as `${route.id}`.

A site's pages may be separate documents (one file per page, checked and rendered together); `navigate` then
names a canvas id of another document. Give a canvas a `"path"` (`"pricing"`, a top-level key of the canvas
node, not a prop) for its URL; without one it gets a path from its name. The first screen of the first document
is the entry screen.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["home", "about", "signup"],
  "nodes": {
    "home": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "slots": {"body": "homeCol"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "homeCol": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["toAbout", "openSignup", "toast"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "toAbout": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "About us"},
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "navigate", "to": "about"}]}]
    },
    "openSignup": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Sign up"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "openModal", "to": "signup", "presentation": "dialog"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "toast": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Show a toast"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "showToast", "message": "Saved", "style": "success"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "about": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "About",
      "path": "about",
      "slots": {"body": "aboutCol"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF9FAFB"}]}
    },
    "aboutCol": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["aboutTitle", "back"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "aboutTitle": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 30}},
      "props": {"text": "About", "style": {"fontSize": 24, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "back": {
      "type": "textButton",
      "layout": {"width": 120, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Back"},
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "navigate", "mode": "pop"}]}]
    },
    "signup": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Sign up",
      "slots": {"body": "signupCol"},
      "layout": {"width": 320, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "signupCol": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["signupTitle", "close"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 320}, "height": {"fill": 200}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 16}
    },
    "signupTitle": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 26}},
      "props": {"text": "Join the waitlist", "style": {"fontSize": 20, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "close": {
      "type": "filledButton",
      "layout": {"width": 120, "height": 40},
      "props": {"label": "Close"},
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "closeModal"}]}]
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-responsive"></a>
## 7. Responsive design

The project's **breakpoints** name size classes by minimum width. Unless a document's `breakpoints` key says
otherwise they are:

| id | name | minWidth | design width × height |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile` | Mobile | 0 | 390 × 844 |
| `tablet` | Tablet | 600 | 834 × 1112 |
| `desktop` | Desktop | 1024 | 1440 × 900 |

There are three tools, which combine:

1. **Fluid layout inside one canvas**: `fill` widths, `constraints.maxWidth`, `wrap` rows. Good for small
   differences.
2. **A canvas per breakpoint.** Canvases with the same `props.screen` are one screen; each sets
   `props.breakpoint` to the breakpoint it is the design for. At a given window width the screen shows the canvas
   whose breakpoint's `minWidth` is the highest at or below the width, else its narrowest. So with mobile and
   desktop canvases only, an 834 wide tablet shows the mobile canvas. Each canvas has its own nodes (its own ids);
   share state between them with `page_variables` ([section 8](#guide-variables)).
3. **A `variance` node**: one node whose `props.variants` each list children for a breakpoint
   (`{"id", "name", "breakpoint", "children": [...]}`); it shows the variant of the current breakpoint, else of the
   widest narrower one, else the narrowest. Its `children` lists every variant's children.

`${screen}` describes the window in expressions: `screen.width`, `screen.height`, `screen.breakpoint` (the id),
`screen.isMobile`, `screen.isTablet`, `screen.isDesktop` (one per breakpoint id), `screen.atLeast.tablet`,
`screen.is.mobile`. `${screen.width}` prints a decimal (`390.0`); `${= screen.width}` prints `390`.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["home-mobile", "home-desktop"],
  "nodes": {
    "home-mobile": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "props": {"screen": "home", "breakpoint": "mobile"},
      "slots": {"body": "m-page"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "m-page": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["m-title", "m-size"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 8}
    },
    "m-title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 32}},
      "props": {"text": "Stacked for phones", "style": {"fontSize": 24, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "m-size": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {
        "text": "${screen.breakpoint}: ${screen.width} px wide",
        "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF6B7280"}
      }
    },
    "home-desktop": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "name": "Home",
      "props": {"screen": "home", "breakpoint": "desktop"},
      "slots": {"body": "d-page"},
      "layout": {"width": 1440, "height": 900},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF3F4F6"}]}
    },
    "d-page": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["d-title", "d-size"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 1440}, "height": {"hug": 120}, "padding": 48},
      "props": {"mainAxisAlignment": "spaceBetween"}
    },
    "d-title": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 400}, "height": {"hug": 48}},
      "props": {"text": "Side by side on desktops", "style": {"fontSize": 40, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "d-size": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {
        "text": "${screen.breakpoint}: ${screen.width} px wide",
        "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF6B7280"}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["page"],
  "nodes": {
    "page": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["features"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24}
    },
    "features": {
      "type": "variance",
      "children": ["stacked", "sideBySide"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 200}},
      "props": {
        "variants": [
          {"id": "narrow", "name": "Narrow", "breakpoint": "mobile", "children": ["stacked"]},
          {"id": "wide", "name": "Wide", "breakpoint": "tablet", "children": ["sideBySide"]}
        ]
      }
    },
    "stacked": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["a1", "a2"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 100}},
      "props": {"spacing": 12}
    },
    "a1": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF6366F1"}], "radius": 8}
    },
    "a2": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF22C55E"}], "radius": 8}
    },
    "sideBySide": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["b1", "b2"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 80}},
      "props": {"spacing": 12}
    },
    "b1": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 100}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF6366F1"}], "radius": 8}
    },
    "b2": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 100}, "height": 80},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF22C55E"}], "radius": 8}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-variables"></a>
## 8. Variables, bindings and expressions

**Variables** hold a screen's state. Declare them in the document's `variables`, under a canvas id (that canvas
only) or under `"page_variables"` (every canvas of the document, kept while the user moves between them):

```json
"variables": {"page_variables": [{"name": "annual", "type": "boolean", "value": false}]}
```

Types: `integer`, `text`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `color`, `list`, `map`, `image`, `choice`. `value` is written as the type holds it in JSON: `3`, `2.5`, `true`, `"text"`,
`"#FF2563EB"`, `[...]`, `{...}`.

**Expressions** are text that reads values:

- `${name}` or `${path}` reads a value: `${count}`, `${user.name}`, `${items[0].price}`, `${item.title}`.
- `${= formula}` computes one: `${= count * price}`, `${= annual ? 'Yearly' : 'Monthly'}`,
  `${= money(total, '$')}`. Operators: `+ - * / %`, comparisons, `&&`, `||`, `!`, `a ? b : c`; functions are
  listed in [formula functions](#page-formulas).
- A text that is exactly one expression gives its value with its type (a number stays a number, a list a list);
  any other text with `${...}` is text with the values inserted.

Names an expression can start with: the screen's variables and `data`, `route`, `storage`, `screen`, `theme`, `item`, `index`, `parent`, `result`, `loop`, `auth`, `drag`, `perf`, `track`, `dismiss`, `pan`, `transform`, `flip`, `tilt`, `view`, `sticky`, `script`, `speech`, `pageOffset`. `screen` and `route` are described
above; `item` and `index` exist inside a list's item ([section 13](#guide-lists)); `result` is what the previous
action of a chain gave.

**Bindings** put an expression on a field. `bind` maps a **binding path** to an expression; the field takes the
value whenever the names it reads change:

```json
"bind": {"props.text": "${= 'Total: ' + money(count * price, '$')}", "visible": "${= count > 0}"}
```

Paths: `visible`, `opacity`, `layout.<field>` (`layout.width`), `decoration.fills[0].color`,
`decoration.radius`, `props.<prop>` and `props.<prop>.<field>` (`props.style.color`), `data` (a list's items),
`selected`, `disabled`, and behavior keys. Full list: [bindings](#page-bindings). Values are read loosely
(`"12"` is a number, `"#FF0000"` a color); a value that cannot be read leaves the field as it was. A text's
`props.text` may hold `${...}` directly, without `bind`. Other fields do not evaluate expressions written in them:
`"opacity": "${x}"` is an error; write `"bind": {"opacity": "${x}"}`.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["counter"],
  "nodes": {
    "counter": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["label", "total", "add"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 400}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "label": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"text": "Clicked ${count} times", "style": {"fontSize": 18, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "total": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF6B7280"}},
      "bind": {"props.text": "${= 'Total: ' + money(count * price, '$')}"}
    },
    "add": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": 160, "height": 44},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 8},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "count", "op": "add", "value": "1"}]
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "counter": [{"name": "count", "type": "integer", "value": 0}, {"name": "price", "type": "decimal", "value": 2.5}]
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-conditions"></a>
## 9. Conditions

A condition sets node fields while a test holds: an ordered list of branches (if, else if, ..., else). It lives
in the document's `conditions`, under a canvas id. Each branch has `when` (a predicate; none for the final else)
and `set`, a list of `{"node": id, "path": binding path, "value": value}`. A predicate is
`{"left": "${annual}", "op": "isTrue"}`, `{"left": "${count}", "op": "greaterThan", "right": "5"}`, or
`{"and": [...]}` / `{"or": [...]}`.

| op | Reads right | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `equalsTo` | yes |  |
| `notEqualsTo` | yes |  |
| `greaterThan` | yes |  |
| `lessThan` | yes |  |
| `greaterThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `lessThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `isEmpty` | no | Null, or an empty text, list or map. |
| `isNotEmpty` | no |  |
| `contains` | yes | A list holds the right operand, a text contains it, a map has it as a key. |
| `isOdd` | no |  |
| `isEven` | no |  |
| `isNull` | no | Null, or the text `null`. |
| `isTrue` | no |  |
| `isFalse` | no |  |

For one field the first branch that holds and sets it wins; a condition wins over the node's binding, which wins
over the node's own value. A binding with a formula is often simpler; conditions suit setting several nodes at
once.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["plans"],
  "nodes": {
    "plans": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["toggle", "price", "note"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 300}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "toggle": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["toggleLabel"],
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": {"hug": 36}, "padding": [14, 8, 14, 8]},
      "decoration": {"strokes": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 18},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "annual", "op": "toggle"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "toggleLabel": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Monthly", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF2563EB"}},
      "bind": {"props.text": "${= annual ? 'Annual billing' : 'Monthly billing'}"}
    },
    "price": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 40}},
      "props": {"text": "$12 / month", "style": {"fontSize": 32, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "note": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 80}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Save 20% with annual billing", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF16A34A"}}
    }
  },
  "variables": {"plans": [{"name": "annual", "type": "boolean", "value": false}]},
  "conditions": {
    "plans": [
      {
        "id": "billing",
        "branches": [
          {
            "when": {"left": "${annual}", "op": "isTrue"},
            "set": [
              {"node": "price", "path": "props.text", "value": "$120 / year"},
              {"node": "note", "path": "visible", "value": false}
            ]
          },
          {"set": [{"node": "price", "path": "props.text", "value": "$12 / month"}]}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-reactions"></a>
## 10. Reactions: triggers and actions

A node's `actions` is a list of **reactions**. A reaction is a **trigger** and the chain of **actions** it runs, in
order:

```json
"actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"},
             "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "count", "op": "add", "value": "1"},
                         {"type": "navigate", "to": "thanks"}]}]
```

- Triggers ([all](#page-triggers)): `click`, `hover`, `cursorEnter`/`cursorExit`, `longPress`, `changed`
  (an input's value changed), `submitted`, `load` (on a canvas: the screen appeared), `valueChanged` (a variable
  changed), `timer`, `scroll`, `enterViewport`... A trigger may be written as just its type: `"trigger": "click"`.
- Actions ([all](#page-actions)) include `setVariable` (`op`: `set` (default), `toggle`, `add`, `subtract`,
  `insert`, `removeAt`...; `value` is an expression), `navigate`, `openModal`, `closeModal`, `showToast`,
  `openLink` (`url`), `if` (`condition`: a predicate; `then` and `else`: action lists), `delay` (`ms`),
  `scrollTo` (`node`), `setValue`, `submitForm`, `callApi`.
- In a chain `${result}` is what the previous action (first: the trigger's event) gave: for a text field's
  `changed`, its text.
- Every action also takes `enabled`, `nonBlocking` and `when` (a predicate: run only while it holds).

Write each action's fields flat in the action object, exactly as named in [actions](#page-actions);
a misspelled key is dropped silently by the runtime and reported by validation (`unknown_action_key`).

<a id="guide-states"></a>
## 11. Hover, press and other states

`states` on a node changes it and its descendants while it is `hovered`, `pressed`, `focused`, `selected`,
`disabled` or `dragged`. Each state maps node ids (the node itself or nodes inside it) to a **patch**: partial node
JSON merged over that node (objects merge, other values replace, `null` removes).

`selected` and `disabled` follow bindings: `"bind": {"selected": "${= tab == 'pricing'}"}` puts the node in its
`selected` state. `hovered` needs a mouse: on touch screens it never happens, so do not hide anything behind it.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["buttons"],
  "nodes": {
    "buttons": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["cta"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 200}},
      "props": {"mainAxisAlignment": "center"}
    },
    "cta": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["ctaLabel"],
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 160}, "height": {"hug": 44}, "padding": [20, 12, 20, 12]},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF2563EB"}], "radius": 10},
      "states": {
        "hovered": {
          "cta": {"decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FF1D4ED8"}]}},
          "ctaLabel": {"props": {"text": "Let's go"}}
        },
        "pressed": {"cta": {"opacity": 0.8}}
      },
      "actions": [{"trigger": {"type": "click"}, "actions": [{"type": "openLink", "url": "https://example.com"}]}]
    },
    "ctaLabel": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Get started", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FFFFFFFF"}}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-scrolling"></a>
## 12. Scrolling

A screen scrolls only if something in it scrolls. Make the canvas's body column scroll:
`"props": {"scrollable": true}` with `{"fill": n}` width and height. Its children keep their sizes and the column
scrolls when they are taller than the screen. Without it, content past the bottom of the screen is cut off on a
device (the render command reports `offscreen`). Inside a scrolling column, a child cannot `fill` the scrolling
axis (there is no end to fill to). Rows scroll sideways with `"scrollable": true, "scrollDirection": "horizontal"`.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["article"],
  "nodes": {
    "article": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "scroller"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 844},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "scroller": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["header", "p1", "p2", "p3"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 844}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"scrollable": true, "spacing": 16, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "header": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 400},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFDBEAFE"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p1": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFDE68A"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p2": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 300},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFBBF7D0"}], "radius": 16}
    },
    "p3": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "The end of the page.", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-lists"></a>
## 13. Lists and repeated data

A `listView` (or `gridView`, `pageView`) repeats its **first child** once per item of its `data` binding:
`"bind": {"data": "${questions}"}`. Inside the repeated child, `${item}` is the item (`${item.title}`) and `${index}`
its position from 0. A list in a scrolling page sets `"scrollable": false` so it lays out every item at its full
height; `spacing` separates items. Items fill the list's width.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["faq"],
  "nodes": {
    "faq": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 600},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["heading", "items"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 600}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start", "scrollable": true}
    },
    "heading": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 30}},
      "props": {"text": "Questions", "style": {"fontSize": 24, "fontWeight": 700, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "items": {
      "type": "listView",
      "children": ["item"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 300}},
      "props": {"scrollable": false, "spacing": 8},
      "bind": {"data": "${questions}"}
    },
    "item": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["q", "a"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 60}, "padding": 12},
      "props": {"crossAxisAlignment": "start", "spacing": 4},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFF3F4F6"}], "radius": 8},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "open", "value": "${= open == index ? -1 : index}"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "q": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 318}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.q}", "style": {"fontSize": 16, "fontWeight": 600, "color": "#FF111827"}}
    },
    "a": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 318}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "${item.a}", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "height": 1.4, "color": "#FF4B5563"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${= open == index}"}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "faq": [
      {"name": "open", "type": "integer", "value": -1},
      {
        "name": "questions",
        "type": "list",
        "value": [
          {"q": "Can I cancel any time?", "a": "Yes. Your plan stays active until the end of the period."},
          {"q": "Do you offer refunds?", "a": "Within 14 days of purchase, no questions asked."},
          {"q": "Is there a free trial?", "a": "Every plan starts with 30 days free."}
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The same item template can carry reactions: a click on an item runs with that item's `item` and `index`.

<a id="guide-forms"></a>
## 14. Forms and inputs

Inputs are Material widgets: `textField`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `radio`, `slider`, `dropdown`,
`segmentedButton`, `datePicker`. Each reports its value through its `changed` trigger as `${result}`; store it in a
variable with `setVariable`. A text field's label and hint are in `props.decoration`
([InputDecoration](#type-InputDecoration): `labelText`, `hintText`, `helperText`, `filled`,
`fillColor`, `border`...).

Validate with variables: keep the values, set a `tried` flag on submit, and show error texts with `visible`
bindings (or bind `props.decoration.errorText`). The `validator` prop of a text field is declared but not applied
by the SDK, and `inputFormatter` only applies `{"type": "regex", "pattern": ..., "allow": true}`. An outlined
field (`"border": {"type": "outline", ...}`) needs `"contentPadding": [14, 16, 14, 16]` in its decoration to keep
its text off the border. A text field is not bound to its variable: setting the variable does not change the
text shown.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["contact"],
  "nodes": {
    "contact": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 500},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["email", "emailError", "send", "thanks"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 500}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 8, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "email": {
      "type": "textField",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 56},
      "props": {"decoration": {"labelText": "Email", "hintText": "you@example.com"}, "keyboardType": "emailAddress"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "changed"},
          "actions": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "email", "value": "${result}"}]
        }
      ]
    },
    "emailError": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 18}},
      "props": {"text": "Enter a valid email address.", "style": {"fontSize": 13, "color": "#FFDC2626"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${= tried && !contains(email, '@')}"}
    },
    "send": {
      "type": "elevatedButton",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 120}, "height": 44},
      "props": {"label": "Send"},
      "actions": [
        {
          "trigger": {"type": "click"},
          "actions": [
            {"type": "setVariable", "variable": "tried", "value": "true"},
            {
              "type": "if",
              "condition": {"left": "${= contains(email, '@')}", "op": "isTrue"},
              "then": [{"type": "setVariable", "variable": "sent", "value": "true"}]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "thanks": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "Thanks! We'll reply within a day.", "style": {"fontSize": 15, "color": "#FF16A34A"}},
      "bind": {"visible": "${sent}"}
    }
  },
  "variables": {
    "contact": [
      {"name": "email", "type": "text", "value": ""},
      {"name": "tried", "type": "boolean", "value": false},
      {"name": "sent", "type": "boolean", "value": false}
    ]
  }
}
```

Buttons (`elevatedButton`, `filledButton`, `outlinedButton`, `textButton`) take `label` and `style`
([ButtonStyle](#type-ButtonStyle): `backgroundColor`, `foregroundColor`, `textStyle`, `shape`...).
Their label text is 12 px unless `style.textStyle.fontSize` says otherwise. Give buttons a fixed width: a hugging
button is only as wide as its label, without padding. For full control of a button's look, use a `row` with a
decoration, padding, a text child and a `click` reaction, as in [section 11](#guide-states).

<a id="guide-modals"></a>
## 15. Modals and toasts

`{"type": "openModal", "to": "<canvas id>"}` shows another canvas over the screen, at its design size
(`presentation`: `dialog`, `bottomSheet`, `fullScreen`...). Inside it, `{"type": "closeModal"}` closes it. The modal
canvas is a root like any screen; give it the size of the dialog.
`{"type": "showToast", "message": "Saved", "style": "success"}` shows a short message.
See the navigation example in [section 6](#guide-screens).

<a id="guide-images"></a>
## 16. Images, icons and fonts

- **Images** are image fills: `{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "...", "fit": "cover"}}` in `decoration.fills`
  of a box (give the box the image's size or an `aspectRatio`). The SDK loads `https://` URLs and `data:image/...`
  URLs. For drafts, the render command also reads a path relative to the document (`"assets/photo.png"`) and
  inlines it; a real publish needs the image uploaded and its URL. The render command does not fetch network
  images: it reports them (`image_network`) and leaves them blank.
- **Icons**: an `icon` node with `props.icon` set to a Material icon name (`"check_circle"`, `"menu"`,
  `"arrow_forward"`; `_outlined`, `_rounded`, `_sharp` suffixes pick the style) and `props.color`.
- **Fonts**: `style.fontFamily` names a family (`"Inter"`), with `fontWeight` choosing the file. An app fetches
  Google Fonts by name. The render command uses font files from `--fonts <dir>` (read by their real family and
  weight) plus Roboto, and reports a family it does not have (`font_fallback`).

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "roots": ["gallery"],
  "nodes": {
    "gallery": {
      "type": "canvas",
      "slots": {"body": "col"},
      "layout": {"width": 390, "height": 360},
      "decoration": {"fills": [{"color": "#FFFFFFFF"}]}
    },
    "col": {
      "type": "column",
      "children": ["photo", "caption"],
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 390}, "height": {"fill": 360}, "padding": 24},
      "props": {"spacing": 12, "crossAxisAlignment": "start"}
    },
    "photo": {
      "type": "box",
      "layout": {"width": {"fill": 342}, "height": 200},
      "decoration": {
        "fills": [{"type": "image", "image": {"url": "assets/photo.png", "fit": "cover"}}],
        "radius": 12,
        "clip": "antiAlias"
      }
    },
    "caption": {
      "type": "row",
      "children": ["check", "captionText"],
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 200}, "height": {"hug": 24}},
      "props": {"spacing": 6}
    },
    "check": {
      "type": "icon",
      "layout": {"width": 20, "height": 20},
      "props": {"icon": "check_circle", "color": "#FF16A34A"}
    },
    "captionText": {
      "type": "text",
      "layout": {"width": {"hug": 100}, "height": {"hug": 20}},
      "props": {"text": "An image fill and a Material icon", "style": {"fontSize": 14, "color": "#FF374151"}}
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="guide-checking"></a>
## 17. Checking your work

Decoding is lenient: a misspelled key, a value of the wrong shape or an unknown enum value is silently ignored or
replaced by its default. Never trust a document that has not been checked.

Run the render command from the SDK repository (`tool/render/README.md` there has the details):

```sh
tool/render/render.sh site/ --out shots/ --sizes 390x844,834x1112,1440x900 --full-page
```

It validates every document strictly, renders each screen with the SDK at each size, writes
`shots/<screen>@<w>x<h>.png` and `shots/diagnostics.json`, and prints one line per problem with a code, the
JSON pointer of the value (`/nodes/hero-title/props/style/fontSize`) and what to do. It exits 1 when there are
errors. Interactions before the capture: `--tap <id>` (scrolled into view first; `<id>#<n>` for the n-th copy
of a list item), `--hover <id>`, `--set <variable>=<json>`, `--scroll <id or screen>=<px>`,
`--navigate <canvas id>`, `--wait <ms>`, with `--label <name>` to keep the screenshots apart. Look at the screenshots: validation cannot tell you that a page is ugly.

Validation codes (from `package:codelessly_api/validate.dart`):

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_document` | error | The document is not a JSON object, or a top-level key has the wrong shape (nodes not an object, roots not a list). |
| `schema_version` | warning | The document has no "schema": 2, or another version. |
| `unknown_document_key` | error | A top-level key of the document that nothing reads. |
| `dangling_root` | error | A root id that names no node. |
| `root_not_canvas` | warning | A root that is not a canvas: it is never shown as a screen. |
| `no_roots` | error | The document has no roots, so nothing is shown. |
| `invalid_node` | error | A node that is not an object or has no "type": decoding drops it. |
| `unknown_node_type` | error | A node type no declaration knows: it renders as an empty box. |
| `unknown_node_key` | error | A key on a node that is neither a node field nor a behavior: it is kept but does nothing. |
| `unknown_prop` | error | A key in "props" that the node type does not declare: it does nothing. |
| `unknown_layout_key` | error | A key in "layout" that layout does not read. |
| `unknown_decoration_key` | error | A key in "decoration" that decoration does not read. |
| `unknown_field` | error | A key inside a value (a paint, a text style, a behavior model...) that its type does not read. |
| `wrong_type` | error | A value of the wrong JSON type or shape: decoding ignores it and uses the default. |
| `loose_value` | warning | A value of another JSON type that decoding converts (the text "12" for a number): write the type itself. |
| `invalid_enum` | error | A value that is not one of the allowed names: decoding uses the default. |
| `out_of_range` | error | A number outside its declared bounds: decoding clamps it. |
| `decoration_ignored` | warning | Fills, strokes, radius or shadows on a type without a box decoration: only blur effects are kept. |
| `dangling_child` | error | A child id that names no node. |
| `dangling_slot` | error | A slot whose id names no node. |
| `multiple_parents` | error | A node listed as a child (or slot) of more than one parent, or twice in one parent. |
| `cycle` | error | A node that contains itself. |
| `unreachable_node` | warning | A node no root reaches: it is never shown. |
| `unknown_slot` | error | A slot name the node type does not have. |
| `children_not_allowed` | error | A "children" list on a type that takes none (or takes slots only): they are never shown. |
| `slots_not_allowed` | error | A "slots" map on a type that has no slots. |
| `canvas_as_child` | error | A canvas used as the child of another node: canvases are screens, only roots. |
| `layout_field_ignored` | warning | A layout field the node's parent does not read (x/y outside a stack, flex/align outside a row or column). |
| `fit_not_allowed` | warning | A width or height mode the parent cannot honor (fill along a scrolling axis, flexible outside a row/column). |
| `zero_size` | warning | A fixed width or height of 0 (often a missing "width"/"height"): the node is invisible. |
| `unknown_bind_path` | error | A "bind" key that names no bindable field of the node. |
| `reserved_bind_path` | warning | A binding path that is kept but not applied yet. |
| `expression_syntax` | error | A "${" that is not closed, or an empty ${}. |
| `unknown_name` | error | An expression reads a name that is neither a declared variable nor a scope the runtime provides. |
| `unknown_trigger` | error | A reaction whose trigger type is unknown or missing: the reaction is dropped. |
| `unknown_trigger_key` | error | A key of a trigger that triggers do not read. |
| `unknown_action_type` | error | An action type no declaration knows: the runtime skips it. |
| `unknown_action_key` | error | A key of an action that its type does not read. |
| `unknown_target_node` | error | An action or condition names a node id that is not in the document. |
| `unknown_screen` | error | A navigate or openModal names a screen (canvas or layout id) that does not exist. |
| `unknown_variable` | error | An action or trigger names a variable that is not declared. |
| `invalid_reaction` | error | A reaction or action that is not an object, or an action list that is not a list. |
| `invalid_variable` | error | A variable without a name, with an unknown type, or whose value its type cannot hold. |
| `duplicate_variable` | error | Two variables of the same name in one scope. |
| `unknown_scope` | error | Variables or conditions keyed by an id that is not a canvas of the document (nor page_variables). |
| `invalid_condition` | error | A condition, branch, predicate or set entry of the wrong shape. |
| `unknown_breakpoint` | error | A canvas or variant names a breakpoint id the project does not define. |
| `duplicate_breakpoint_canvas` | error | Two canvases of one screen are the design for the same breakpoint. |
| `screen_without_breakpoint` | warning | A canvas grouped into a screen (props.screen) that names no breakpoint: it shows only below the narrowest. |
| `duplicate_id` | warning | The same node id in two documents of one project: each document keeps its own, but reports and the render command's steps name nodes by id. |

The render step adds what only rendering shows: `render_exception`, `action_error`, `interaction_failed`,
`layout_overflow`, `offscreen`, `text_clipped`, `text_truncated`, `text_no_color`, `font_fallback`,
`image_failed`, `image_network`, `empty_screen`, `invalid_json`; formulas are parsed by the SDK's own parser
there, so formula syntax errors and unknown names in formulas are reported only by the render command.

<a id="guide-pitfalls"></a>
## 18. Rules that are easy to get wrong

1. Every node needs `layout.width` and `layout.height`; without them it is 0 × 0.
2. Every text needs `style.color`; without it, it is white.
3. Padding and margin are a number or four numbers, never two.
4. Colors are `#AARRGGBB` or `#RRGGBB`.
5. Columns center their children across by default: write `"crossAxisAlignment": "start"` for left-aligned
   content.
6. A screen taller than the window needs a scrolling body column.
7. Values in `props`, `layout` and `decoration` are literal; expressions go in `bind` (except `props.text`).
8. `x`/`y` only work under a `stack`; `flex`/`align` only under a `row` or `column`.
9. Ids are map keys; a child is listed in exactly one parent; canvases are only in `roots`.
10. Per-breakpoint canvases have separate nodes: shared state lives in `page_variables`.
11. `fill` takes all the room it is given; cap it with `constraints.maxWidth`.
12. A backslash inside a formula is written twice in JSON: `"${= matches(code, '^\\d{4}$')}"`.

<a id="node-canvas"></a>
## `canvas`

Flutter `Scaffold`.

- Children: slots: `body`, `appBar`, `floatingActionButton`, `bottomNavigationBar`.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).

- `scaleMode`: [ScaleMode](#enum-ScaleMode) = `"responsive"` (`responsive`, `autoScale`)
- `blockBack`: bool = `false`
- `breakpoint`: String = `""`
- `screen`: String = `""`
- `breakpointMinWidth`: double = unset (≥ 0)
- `overlay`: bool = `false`
- `backdrop`: bool = `false`

<a id="node-stack"></a>
## `stack`

Flutter `Stack`.

- Children: `children`.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).
- Reads from each child's layout: [`x`](#layout-x), [`y`](#layout-y).

- `scrollable`: bool = `false`
- `scrollDirection`: [Axis](#enum-Axis) = `"vertical"` (`horizontal`, `vertical`)
- `reverse`: bool = `false`
- `physics`: [ScrollPhysicsType](#enum-ScrollPhysicsType) = `"platform"` (`platform`, `bouncing`, `clamping`, `never`, `rangeMaintaining`)
- `alwaysScroll`: bool = `false`
- `clipBehavior`: [Clip](#enum-Clip) = `"hardEdge"` (`none`, `hardEdge`, `antiAlias`, `antiAliasWithSaveLayer`)
- `fit`: [BoxFit](#enum-BoxFit) = unset (`fill`, `contain`, `cover`, `fitWidth`, `fitHeight`, `none`, `scaleDown`)
- `fitAlignment`: [Alignment](#type-Alignment) = `[0,0]`

<a id="node-box"></a>
## `box`

Flutter `Container`.

- Children: none.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).

- `path`: String = `""`
- `strokeJoin`: [StrokeJoin](#enum-StrokeJoin) = `"miter"` (`miter`, `round`, `bevel`)
- `strokeMiterLimit`: double = `4` (≥ 0)

<a id="node-row"></a>
## `row`

Flutter `Row`.

- Children: `children`.
- Decoration: box decoration (fills, strokes, radius, shadows, clip).
- Reads from each child's layout: [`flex`](#layout-flex), [`squeezable`](#layout-squeezable), [`align`](#layout-align).

- `mainAxisAlignment`: [MainAxisAlignment](#enum-MainAxisAlignment) = `"start"` (`start`, `end`, `center`, `spaceBetween`, `spaceAround`, `spaceEvenly`)
- `crossAxisAlignment`: [CrossAxisAlignment](#enum-CrossAxisAlignment) = `"center"` (`start`, `end`, `center`, `stretch`, `baseline`)
- `spacing`: double = `0` (≥ 0)
- `wrap`: bool = `false`
- `runSpacing`: double = `0` (≥ 0)
- `squeezeChildren`: bool = `true`
- `scrollable`: bool = `false`

<a id="page-layout"></a>
# Layout

A node's `"layout"` object: its size, spacing, and placement in its parent. See the guide's
[Layout](#guide-layout) section for how the modes behave, with examples.

`width` and `height` are an [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize): a number (fixed) or `{"fill" | "hug" |
"flexible" | "fixed": number}`. `x` and `y` are an [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition). The default
size is fixed 0: a node without a width and a height draws nothing.

## Fields

<a id="layout-width"></a>
<a id="layout-height"></a>
<a id="layout-constraints"></a>
<a id="layout-margin"></a>
<a id="layout-padding"></a>
<a id="layout-rotation"></a>
<a id="layout-aspectRatio"></a>
<a id="layout-flex"></a>
<a id="layout-squeezable"></a>
<a id="layout-x"></a>
<a id="layout-y"></a>
<a id="layout-align"></a>
- `width`: [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize) = `0`
- `height`: [AxisSize](#type-AxisSize) = `0`
- `constraints`: [BoxConstraints](#type-BoxConstraints) = `{}`
- `margin`: [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) = `0`
- `padding`: [EdgeInsets](#type-EdgeInsets) = `0`
- `rotation`: double = `0`
- `aspectRatio`: double = unset (≥ 0)
- `flex`: int = `1` (≥ 0)
- `squeezable`: bool = `false`
- `x`: [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition) = `{"start":0}`
- `y`: [AxisPosition](#type-AxisPosition) = `{"start":0}`
- `align`: [Alignment](#type-Alignment) = unset

Read by decoding but not declared as fields: `widthFactor`, `heightFactor`. A share (0–1 and up) of the room its parent gives it on that axis (`FractionallySizedBox`): a progress bar's fill is `widthFactor: 0.6` of its track. Null: sized by `width` / `height`. Bindable (`layout.widthFactor`).

## Which sizing modes each parent allows

| Parent | Width may be | Height may be |
|---|---|---|
| `row` | fixed, fill, flexible, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, flexible, hug |
| `row` with {"wrap":true} | fixed, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `column` with {"scrollable":true} | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, hug |
| `row` with {"scrollable":true,"scrollDirection":"horizontal"} | fixed, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `stack` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `canvas` | fixed, fill, hug | fixed, fill, hug |
| `listView` | fill | fixed, hug |
| `listView` with {"itemExtent":80} | fill | fill |
| `gridView` | fill | fill |
| `pageView` | fill | fill |

Why a mode is not allowed, as the declarations say it:

- Flexible only applies in a row or column, along its main axis.
- A wrapping row lays its children out in runs: they keep their own size along it.
- The column scrolls: its content has no end to fill to.
- The row scrolls: its content has no end to fill to.
- Items in a list always fill across it.
- A list is unbounded along its scroll axis: items cannot fill it. Set an item extent.
- The list gives every item its item extent: they fill it.
- Grid cells size their children: they fill them.
- Pages size their children: they fill them.

<a id="page-values"></a>
# Value types, models and enums

How values are written in JSON. **Value types** are written in a compact form of their own (a color as
`"#AARRGGBB"`). **Models** are JSON objects with the fields listed. **Enums** are written as the value's name.
Decoding is lenient and never fails: a value it cannot read becomes the field's default, which is why
validation reports it.

## Value types

<a id="type-Alignment"></a>
### Alignment

JSON: [x, y] from -1 to 1, or a name: topLeft, topCenter, topRight, centerLeft, center, centerRight, bottomLeft, bottomCenter, bottomRight.

<a id="type-AxisPosition"></a>
### AxisPosition

JSON: a number (distance from the start) or {"start": d}, {"end": d}, {"start": a, "end": b}, {"align": -1..1}, {"relative": d}.

<a id="type-AxisSize"></a>
### AxisSize

JSON: a number (fixed) or {"fill"|"flexible"|"hug"|"fixed": number}.

<a id="type-BorderRadius"></a>
### BorderRadius

JSON: a number (every corner), [x, y] (every corner elliptical) or [topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft] (each a number or [x, y]).

<a id="type-BoxConstraints"></a>
### BoxConstraints

JSON: {"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"} (each optional, numbers >= 0).

<a id="type-Color"></a>
### Color

JSON: "#AARRGGBB" or "#RRGGBB" (hex, alpha first).

<a id="type-EdgeInsets"></a>
### EdgeInsets

JSON: a number (all sides) or [left, top, right, bottom].

<a id="type-FontFeature"></a>
### FontFeature

JSON: an OpenType tag ("tnum", "ss01") or "tag=value" ("liga=0").

<a id="type-FontWeight"></a>
### FontWeight

JSON: 100, 200 ... 900.

<a id="type-IconData"></a>
### IconData

JSON: a Material icon name ("check_circle", "lock_open_rounded"), an image URL, or {"type": "MATERIAL_ICON", "name", "style"}.

<a id="type-Offset"></a>
### Offset

JSON: [dx, dy].

<a id="type-Rect"></a>
### Rect

JSON: [left, top, width, height].

<a id="type-Size"></a>
### Size

JSON: [width, height].

## Models

Objects with declared fields. Keys not listed are reported by validation (`unknown_field`).

<a id="page-behaviors"></a>
# Behaviors

Behaviors are what a node does beyond its layout and paint: motion, interaction states, tooltips, drag and drop,
scroll effects. Each is a key written directly on the node (not under `props`), sparse: leave it out for none. The
guide's [states](#guide-states) section shows `states`, the most used one.

## Keys

<a id="page-triggers"></a>
# Triggers

A reaction (`"actions": [{"trigger": {...}, "actions": [...]}]` on a node) starts on its trigger. In the chain,
`${result}` first holds the trigger's event (where a click landed, an input's new value). Screen triggers (`load`,
`valueChanged`, `timer`, `keyDown`...) are set on the canvas.

<a id="page-actions"></a>
# Actions

An action is a JSON object `{"type": "<type>", ...fields}`, run in order in a reaction's chain. Text fields are
expressions (`"${count}"`, `"${= a + 1}"`). A field holding nested actions (`then`, `else`, `onSuccess`...) is a
list of actions. A key not listed for the type is dropped by decoding and reported by validation
(`unknown_action_key`).

## Fields every action has

- `enabled`: bool = `true`
- `nonBlocking`: bool = `false`
- `when`: Object = unset

Fields holding nested action chains (a list of actions): `then`, `else`, `actions`, `onSuccess`, `onError`, `cancelActions`.

<a id="page-bindings"></a>
# Bindings and expressions

`"bind"` on a node maps a **binding path** (a path into the node's JSON) to an expression; the field at the path
takes the expression's value. Paths: `visible`, `opacity`, `layout.<field>`, `decoration.<field>` (with
`[index]`, a paint's `id` or `*` into lists), `props.<prop>` and deeper fields of model props, `data`, `selected`,
`disabled`, and the behavior keys. Values are read loosely: `"12"` is a number, `1` and `"true"` are true,
`"#FF0000"` is a color; a value that cannot be read leaves the field as it was.

Expressions: `${path}` reads a value (`user.name`, `items[0].price`, `pal[item.kind]`), `${= formula}` computes
one ([formula functions](#page-formulas)). A binding that is exactly one expression keeps the value's type.

## Named paths

| Path | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `visible` |  |
| `opacity` |  |
| `selected` | Interaction states driven by data: true puts the node in `WidgetState.selected` / `WidgetState.disabled`, so its state styles (`states.selected`, `states.disabled`) patch it and its descendants, as hover and press do (`"selected": "${= item.id == selectedId}"`). |
| `disabled` |  |
| `data` | The items a repeating widget (list, grid, page view) builds one per. |
| `layout.width` |  |
| `layout.height` |  |
| `layout.flex` |  |
| `layout.rotation` |  |
| `layout.margin` |  |
| `layout.padding` |  |
| `layout.x` |  |
| `layout.y` |  |
| `decoration.radius` |  |
| `decoration.strokeWidth` |  |
| `scale` |  |
| `textDirection` |  |

## Every bindable field

- `layout.<field>`: `width`, `height`, `constraints`, `margin`, `padding`, `rotation`, `aspectRatio`, `flex`, `squeezable`, `x`, `y`, `align`, and `widthFactor`, `heightFactor`.
- `decoration.<field>`: `fills`, `strokes`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeAlign`, `strokeSides`, `strokeCap`, `dashPattern`, `radius`, `effects`, `clip`, `blendMode`, `foregroundFills`, `shape`. Inside `fills`, `strokes`, `foregroundFills` and `effects`, select an item by `[index]`, by its `id`, or every item by `*`, then a field of [Paint](#type-Paint) or [Effect](#type-Effect) (`decoration.fills[0].color`, `decoration.effects.*.color`, `.offset.dx`).
- `props.<prop>`: any prop of the node's type ([node types](#page-nodes)), and `props.<prop>.<field>` for a field of a model prop.
- `<behavior>` and `<behavior>.<field>`: `motion`, `scale`, `animations`, `transitions`, `inkWell`, `states`, `tooltip`, `ignorePointer`, `zoomable`, `floating`, `hero`, `flightKey`, `flight`, `draggable`, `dropTarget`, `track`, `dismissible`, `pan`, `reorderHandle`, `reveal`, `strokePath`, `typewriter`, `particles`, `textDirection`, `flip`, `tilt`, `transformGesture`, `sticky`, `viewProgress`, `measure`, `customPaint`.

## Scopes

Names an expression may start with besides the screen's variables: `data`, `route`, `storage`, `screen`, `theme`, `item`, `index`, `parent`, `result`, `loop`, `auth`, `drag`, `perf`, `track`, `dismiss`, `pan`, `transform`, `flip`, `tilt`, `view`, `sticky`, `script`, `speech`, `pageOffset`.

<a id="page-formulas"></a>
# Formula functions

The functions a formula (`${= ...}`) can call, extracted from the SDK's formula engine
(`FormulaEvaluator.functionDocs`). Formulas also have arithmetic (`+ - * / %`), comparisons (`== != < <= > >=`),
`&&`, `||`, `!`, `cond ? a : b`, string and number literals (`'text'`, `"text"`, `3.5`), lists (`[1, 2]`), paths
(`user.name`, `items[0]`), and lambdas for list functions (`x => x.price`).

Formulas are written inside JSON strings, so a backslash in a formula (a regular expression's `\d`) is written
twice in the JSON: `"${= matches(code, '^\\d{4}$')}"`. A text that is exactly one formula keeps the value's type;
inside other text a number is printed without trailing zeros (`${= 2.50}` prints `2.5`).

Source: codelessly_sdk lib/src/runtime/expressions/formula.dart (FormulaEvaluator.functionDocs, FormulaEvaluator.functions).

| Function | Signature | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `left` | `left(text, count)` | `left("MX4821", 2) → MX` |
| `right` | `right(text, count)` | `right("1FUJGLDR5MX4821", 6) → MX4821` |
| `toMap` | `toMap(list, item => key, item => value)` | `toMap(items, i => i.id, i => "pass") → {1a: pass, 1b: pass}` |
| `money` | `money(value, symbol, decimals) or money(value, decimals)` | `money(price) → $1,234.50` |
| `currency` | `currency(value, code, options?)` | `currency(-1234.5, "EUR") → −1.234,50 €; currency(42, "USD", "signed") → +$42.00` |
| `parseAmount` | `parseAmount(text, code)` | `parseAmount("1.234,50", "EUR") → 1234.5` |
| `formatAmount` | `formatAmount(text, code)` | `formatAmount("12345.6", "USD") → 12,345.6` |
| `currencySymbol` | `currencySymbol(code)` | `currencySymbol("GBP") → £` |
| `currencyDecimals` | `currencyDecimals(code)` | `currencyDecimals("JPY") → 0` |
| `formatNumber` | `formatNumber(value, digits?, locale?)` | `formatNumber(2481.64, 1) → 2,481.6 · formatNumber(1234.5, 1, "ar_EG") → ١٬٢٣٤٫٥` |
| `formatCurrency` | `formatCurrency(value, currencyCode, locale?, decimals?)` | `formatCurrency(1234.5, "EUR", "fr_FR") → 1 234,50 € · formatCurrency(1500, "JPY", "ja_JP") → ￥1,500` |
| `formatPercent` | `formatPercent(value, locale?, decimals?)` | `formatPercent(0.42) → 42% · formatPercent(0.42, "fr_FR") → 42 %` |
| `pluralCategory` | `pluralCategory(count, locale?)` | `pluralCategory(3, "ar") → few · pluralCategory(0, "en") → other` |
| `textDirection` | `textDirection(locale)` | `textDirection("he_IL") → rtl · textDirection("fr") → ltr` |
| `textDirectionOf` | `textDirectionOf(text)` | `textDirectionOf("שלום") → rtl · textDirectionOf("123") → (empty)` |
| `fill` | `fill(template, map or list)` | `fill("{i} of {n}", {i: 1, n: 10}) → 1 of 10` |
| `feetInches` | `feetInches(feet)` | `feetInches(6.67) → 6′ 8″` |
| `fixed` | `fixed(value, decimals)` | `fixed(4.5, 2) → 4.50` |
| `round` | `round(value, decimals)` | `round(4.567, 1) → 4.6` |
| `floor` | `floor(value)` | `floor(4.7) → 4` |
| `ceil` | `ceil(value)` | `ceil(4.2) → 5` |
| `abs` | `abs(value)` | `abs(-3) → 3` |
| `min` | `min(a, b, …) or min(list)` | `min(3, 7) → 3` |
| `max` | `max(a, b, …) or max(list)` | `max(3, 7) → 7` |
| `sum` | `sum(list, field or item => value)` | `sum(cart, i => i.price * i.qty) → 24` |
| `count` | `count(list, item => condition) or count(list, field, value)` | `count(tasks, t => !t.done) → 2` |
| `length` | `length(text or list)` | `length(cart) → 3` |
| `if` | `if(condition, then, else)` | `if(qty > 1, "items", "item")` |
| `plural` | `plural(count, one, many) or plural(count, forms, locale?)` | `plural(2, "photo") → photos · plural(2, {one: "{n} phrase", other: "{n} phrases"}, "en") → 2 phrases` |
| `join` | `join(list, separator, field or item => value)` | `join(tags, " · ")` |
| `upper` | `upper(text)` | `upper("hi") → HI` |
| `charCode` | `charCode(text, index)` | `charCode("MX", 1) → 88` |
| `fromCharCode` | `fromCharCode(code, …) or fromCharCode(list)` | `fromCharCode(65 + seat) → B` |
| `lower` | `lower(text)` | `lower("Hi") → hi` |
| `codeUnits` | `codeUnits(text)` | `sum(codeUnits(tag)) % 8 → a stable color index for tag` |
| `trim` | `trim(text)` | `trim("  hi ") → hi` |
| `contains` | `contains(text or list, value)` | `contains(lower(title), lower(search)) → true` |
| `startsWith` | `startsWith(text, prefix)` | `startsWith("Buy milk", "Buy") → true` |
| `endsWith` | `endsWith(text, suffix)` | `endsWith("photo.png", ".png") → true` |

| `duration` | `duration(seconds)` | `duration(225) → 3:45` |
| `luminance` | `luminance(color)` | `luminance("#FFFFFF") → 1` |
| `filter` | `filter(list, item => condition) or filter(list, field, value)` | `filter(tasks, t => contains(lower(t.title), lower(search)))` |
| `where` | `where(list, field, value) or where(list, item => condition)` | `where(tasks, "done", false)` |
| `find` | `find(list, item => condition) or find(list, field, value)` | `find(users, u => u.id == userId)` |

<a id="page-variables-conditions-scripts"></a>
# Variables, conditions and scripts

Variables, conditions and scripts live at the top of a layout document, keyed by canvas id
(`"variables": {"<canvas id>" | "page_variables": [...]}`, `"conditions": {"<canvas id>": [...]}`), or as a list
(`"scripts"`). See the guide's [variables](#guide-variables) and
[conditions](#guide-conditions) sections for examples.

## Variable fields

| Key | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `"v1"` |  |
| `name` | `"count"` | Unique in its scope; what expressions read (`${name}`). |
| `type` | `"integer"` |  |
| `value` | `3` | The default value, as `type` holds it (see `VariableType.coerce`); null when unset. |
| `formula` | `"a + 1"` | The expression (what goes in `${= ...}`) that computes the value of a computed variable; empty for a plain one. A computed variable is read-only: it changes when what its formula reads changes. |
| `parameters` | `["a"]` | A computed variable with parameters is a function: formulas call it by name (`clamp01(x)`), and its `formula` reads the arguments by these names. |
| `options` | `["a"]` | The options of a `VariableType.choice` variable. |
| `persist` | `true` | Whether the app keeps the value on the device: it starts from the value it had last time (not `value`) and every change is saved. A draft, a list the user builds up. A computed variable can't persist (`persists`). |

### Variable types

`integer`, `text`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `color`, `list`, `map`, `image`, `choice`

## Conditions

An if / else-if / else rule. Its first branch whose test holds and that sets a property gives the property its value; when none does, the property keeps its binding's or its own value. JSON:

```json
{"id": "c1", "name": "Low stock", "branches": [
  {"when": {"left": "${stock}", "op": "lessThan", "right": "5"},
   "set": [{"node": "badge", "path": "visible", "value": true}]},
  {"set": [{"node": "badge", "path": "visible", "value": false}]}]}

```

- Branch: One branch: when `when` holds (always, for an `else`: null), the properties in `sets` take their values.
- Set entry: Sets property `path` (a binding path, DESIGN.md §5.1) of node `node` to `value`: a JSON value, where a string is an expression read like a binding's (`${= qty * 2}`, `#FF0000`, `Hello ${name}`).
- Comparison: `left op right` (the right side only for ops that `ConditionOp.takesRight`).
- Junction: All of `parts` (`and`) or any of them (`or`). Every part is evaluated. JSON: `{"and": [...]}` / `{"or": [...]}`.
- Operand: One side of a `Comparison`: an expression text whose `${...}` are read (`${count}`, `${= a + b}`, `3`, `done`), or, when `raw`, a literal taken as written. Both are then parsed loosely (`3` is a number, `true` a bool, `[1, 2]` a list). JSON: the text, or `{"raw": text}`.

### Comparison ops

| op | Reads right | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `equalsTo` | yes |  |
| `notEqualsTo` | yes |  |
| `greaterThan` | yes |  |
| `lessThan` | yes |  |
| `greaterThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `lessThanOrEqualTo` | yes |  |
| `isEmpty` | no | Null, or an empty text, list or map. |
| `isNotEmpty` | no |  |
| `contains` | yes | A list holds the right operand, a text contains it, a map has it as a key. |
| `isOdd` | no |  |
| `isEven` | no |  |
| `isNull` | no | Null, or the text `null`. |
| `isTrue` | no |  |
| `isFalse` | no |  |

## Scripts

- `id`: String = `""`
- `name`: String = `""`
- `description`: String = `""`
- `params`: Object = unset
- `source`: String = `""`
- `version`: int = `1`
- `capabilities`: List<String> = `[]`
- `timeoutMs`: int = `1000` (≥ 1)
- `memoryLimitMb`: int = `32` (≥ 1)
- `pageId`: String = unset
- `tests`: Object = unset

## Breakpoints

- `id`: String = `""`
- `name`: String = `""`
- `minWidth`: double = `0` (≥ 0)
- `width`: double = `0` (≥ 0)
- `height`: double = `0` (≥ 0)

Defaults:

| id | name | minWidth | design width × height |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile` | Mobile | 0 | 390 × 844 |
| `tablet` | Tablet | 600 | 834 × 1112 |
| `desktop` | Desktop | 1024 | 1440 × 900 |
